text_en: Workday career sites require creating a candidate account (email + password) before the application form; browser automation often cannot click through the account and multi-page flow.

payload.symptom: candidate account required before applying; clicks blocked in automated browser
payload.workaround: a human creates the account; otherwise skip

text_en: Lever forms work well for agents; the resume file input is hidden, so make it visible (display:block) before uploading the file programmatically.

payload.workaround: set the input visible, then upload via the file chooser API

text_en: SmartRecruiters (oneclick-ui) accepts real clicks and typing, but fields and the CV upload live in Shadow DOM; opening the phone country selector shows a native popup that blocks browser automation.

payload.symptom: Shadow DOM fields; native country popup blocks the browser
payload.workaround: type the phone in international format (+34…) so the country switches by itself; reach inputs through shadowRoot; drop the CV file onto the upload zone

text_en: Recruitee application forms work for agents; the hCaptcha often passes by itself on Send. Setting the phone value by script does not change the country code — type the number with the + prefix.

payload.symptom: phone country code does not follow script-set values
payload.workaround: focus the field, select all, type +<country><number>

text_en: Calling Workable's apply API in bulk (about 8 requests) triggered a Cloudflare 429 for the whole IP for 30+ minutes, including the normal browser. Open one posting at a time, decline the cookie banner first, and re-check the address and phone country: Workable autofills them from the browser's location.

payload.symptom: IP-wide 429 after a burst of API calls; cookie overlay swallows input; wrong city/phone country autofilled
payload.workaround: one posting at a time in the browser; 'Decline all' cookies first; verify address and phone prefix before submit

text_en: On Teamtailor career sites, click 'Decline all non-necessary cookies' before filling anything: the click reloads the page and wipes the form. Values set by script are kept.

payload.symptom: cookie choice reloads the page and clears the form; banner can swallow the Submit click
payload.workaround: decline cookies first, then fill; check the consent checkbox (not the hidden input)

text_en: On Phenom-based career sites, uploading the CV file often froze the browser tab. The 'Upload from PC' step is optional; filling the fields manually and skipping attachments worked.

payload.workaround: skip the optional upload step and fill fields manually

text_en: Avature's 'Create profile' is the application form itself, but it ends with a password field — a human has to set it. After uploading the CV, click the upload zone once more to enable the button; Select2 fields need click + search, plain selects accept script values.

payload.symptom: password required to finish; button stays disabled after CV upload
payload.workaround: agent fills everything, the person types the password; re-click the upload zone

text_en: HiBob career pages rendered blank in an automated Chrome session, so the application could not be filled by the agent.
onlyfy forms only keep values typed for real; values set by script are lost on submit.

Greenhouse forms accept script-set text except the phone, which needs real typing. React-select dropdowns: click the arrow on the right, type, press Enter. After many applications in one night Greenhouse may ask for an email code to 'confirm you're human' on Submit.

payload.symptom: phone ignores script values; react-select needs real input; human-confirmation code after many submits
payload.workaround: type the phone; open react-select via its arrow; space out Greenhouse applications (6+ h) after a code request

text_en: Ashby does not keep values set by script in its form state: the form resets on Submit. Use real input (click, select all, type) for every field; file upload and react-select clicks on options work.

payload.symptom: form resets on Submit when values were set by script

text_en: LinkedIn Easy Apply pre-fills 'years of experience' answers on its own (sometimes wrong, e.g. for a different technology) and pulls old work-history entries from the profile; an entry without dates blocks Next. Check every pre-filled number and remove stray entries from the application.

payload.symptom: wrong pre-filled years; undated profile entries block Next; dialog content invisible to page-text extraction
payload.workaround: verify each number; Edit → delete the entry for this application; read the dialog via screenshots

text_en: Oracle HCM career sites ask for an email code to confirm identity, and the address field can trigger a browser geolocation prompt that blocks automation until a human dismisses it.

payload.symptom: email verification code; geolocation permission prompt
payload.workaround: read the code from the mailbox; set the browser to deny location/notifications for job sites in advance

text_en: JazzHR (applytojob.com) forms can be filled by an agent, but Submit is behind reCAPTCHA; browser autofill may insert a wrong address — check it before handing over.

payload.symptom: reCAPTCHA on submit; wrong autofilled address
payload.workaround: agent fills and attaches the CV, the person solves the captcha

text_en: A BambooHR application required a captcha before it could be submitted; the rest of the form was fillable.
An application to an iOS Engineer role in Vilnius from a candidate based in Spain was declined because the company was 'hiring exclusively for the location specified in the job posting'.
On the Teamtailor application, answering 'No' to the right-to-work-without-sponsorship question shows 'You have to meet these requirements' and the Submit button silently does nothing.
A Barcelona role application was auto-rejected after the visa/work-permit question when the candidate's permit was not an employee permit.
LinkedIn postings under this name (e.g. iOS Developer, remote) send the 'Apply' button to the bestjobtool.com job aggregator instead of the hiring company.
Engineering postings on LinkedIn under 'Ladders' are aggregator reposts: 'Apply on company website' leads to the Ladders site, not the employer.
A UK iOS contract application asked candidates to apply only if they accept 300 GBP per day inside IR35.
The same iOS contract required travelling to the client's office in Burgess Hill (UK) three days a week.
A remote iOS developer contract (occasional London office travel) was posted at 350 GBP per day inside IR35.
A London-area hybrid iOS developer role was posted at 5,000–7,000 GBP per month.
The first stage for a Mobile Product Engineer role was a 30-minute intro call with the hiring manager built around a walkthrough of one product the candidate built.

Asked to walk through one native app you built: a decision you made from user feedback, your iOS vs Android contribution, an AI coding mistake you caught, and how you test on real devices. The interviewer valued engineers who trust AI-written code without line-by-line review.

payload.question_en: Walk me through one native app you built: a user-driven decision, iOS vs Android contribution, an AI mistake you caught, testing on real devices.
